REVENUE MODEL          GOVERNANCE MODEL          ATHLETE STATUS
  ─────────────          ────────────────          ──────────────
  1850–1920              1850–1920                 1850–1920
  Gate receipts only     Amateur ideal             "Gentleman" or outcast
  Prize money hidden     IOC/FIFA as moral         Reserve clause / poverty
  Patron subsidy         guardians                 Jim Thorpe stripped
       │                      │                         │
       ▼                      ▼                         ▼
  1920–1960              1920–1960                 1920–1960
  Radio rights ($)       Amateurism enforced       Full-time "amateur"
  Gate still dominant    Brundage era              State-sponsored sham
  Local/regional only    Fear of commercialism     Reserve clause intact
       │                      │                         │
       ▼                      ▼                         ▼
  1960–1980              1960–1980                 1960–1980
  Network TV rights      Cracks appearing          Curt Flood / free agency
  Monday Night Football  Open tennis 1968          NFLPA formed
  ABC/NBC/CBS oligopoly  IOC rule 26 weakening     Union power grows
       │                      │                         │
       ▼                      ▼                         ▼
  1980–2000              1980–2000                 1980–2000
  Cable (ESPN 1979)      Open era arrives          Jordan/Nike brand model
  Sky Sports / BSkyB     Trust funds → open        Bosman ruling (1995)
  Rights auctions begin  IAAF 1982, IOC 1992       Free agency normal
       │                      │                         │
       ▼                      ▼                         ▼
  2000–2015              2000–2015                 2000–2015
  $B rights deals        Analytics enters          Moneyball era
  Global packages        Governance crises         Athlete social media
  Out-of-market bundles  (FIFA corruption etc.)    BALCO/doping arms race
       │                      │                         │
       ▼                      ▼                         ▼
  2015–2024              2015–2024                 2015–2024
  Streaming disruption   Private equity entry      NIL / direct-to-fan
  $50B global industry   Super League (failed)     LeBron's media company
  Live = last DVR-proof  ESG / player activism     Athlete > team brand
